title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District
area: East-central and northeastern Pennsylvania, including Carbon, Columbia, Montour, Northumberland, Schuylkill, Sullivan, and Wyoming counties and parts of Luzerne County.

context.text: Dan Meuser was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Rachel Wallace was unopposed in the Democratic primary after Jennifer Brothers and Daniel Byron did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Dan Meuser is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 9th District, first elected in 2018 and sworn in in 2019. He spent decades at Pride Mobility Products, a power mobility manufacturer, where he served as president of Pride USA, and was Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue from 2011 to 2015. In Congress he serves on the Financial Services and Small Business committees and chairs the Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

background.text: According to his official biography, Meuser is the son of a police officer and attended New York Maritime University and Cornell University, where he was in the Navy ROTC program.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Cornell University in 1986.

Joined Pride Mobility Products in 1988, a healthcare products manufacturer that, according to his official biography, he helped grow into an industry leader in power mobility products; he served as president of Pride USA for seven years.

Served as Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue from 2011 to 2015 under Gov. Tom Corbett (R); his official biography says the Council on State Taxation rated the department as the most improved in the country during his tenure.
Won the open 9th District seat on November 6, 2018, defeating Democrat Denny Wolff, and was sworn in as a member of the 116th Congress in 2019.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and on the Small Business Committee.
Is a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus, Main Street Caucus, Republican Study Committee and Border Security Caucus, and co-chair of the Congressional Coal Caucus.
Lives in Luzerne County with his wife, Shelley; they have two daughters and a son, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to advancing the "America First agenda," including securing the border, promoting American energy dominance, growing the economy, and protecting national security.
priorities.quote: Working alongside President Trump and a unified Republican Congress, I am committed to advancing the America First agenda which the American people voted for.

priorities.text: Lists extending the 2017 Trump tax cuts, expanding small-business access to capital, and supporting domestic natural gas production among his priorities.

positions.summary: Supports reimplementing "Remain in Mexico," ending "Catch and Release," and ensuring Border Patrol agents have resources to stop illegal immigration, drugs, and human trafficking.
positions.quote: Reimplement Remain in Mexico, end Catch and Release.

record.text: Chairs the Committee on Financial Services in the 2025-2026 Congress; also assigned to the Committee on Small Business.

candidates.name: Rachel Wallace
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary unopposed after Jennifer Brothers and Daniel Byron did not make the ballot

summary.text: Rachel Wallace is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 9th District from Pottsville. Her career has been in federal government service, beginning with a job for Rep. Tim Holden in 2010 and including the State Department, the staff of a U.S. Senator and the White House Office of Management and Budget, where she was chief of staff. She is running on lowering the cost of living and health care.

background.text: Born and raised in Pottsville, Pennsylvania, and a graduate of Pottsville Area High School; she describes herself as the daughter of a pastor and a nurse.
Began her career in 2010 working for U.S. Rep. Tim Holden, who represented a former 6th District covering parts of Berks and Schuylkill counties.
Worked at the U.S. State Department from 2014 to 2017.
Served on the staff of a U.S. Senator from 2018 to 2019.
Was chief of staff of the White House Office of Management and Budget from October 2021 to May 2023.
Says she moved back to southern Schuylkill County after her mother was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, to be closer to family that has lived in Berks and Schuylkill counties for 10 generations.
Lives in southern Schuylkill County with her husband and their dog, and describes herself as a social member of her local fire company and gun club.
Announced her candidacy in late September 2025 and advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary; former Rep. Holden has endorsed her.

priorities.text: Says nearly 30,000 people in the district will lose health insurance because of Dan Meuser's votes, and that she will fight to save rural hospitals and end prior-authorization practices.
priorities.quote: Nearly 30,000 people in our part of Pennsylvania will lose their health insurance because of Dan Meuser's votes. Rachel will fight to fix the damage done by Dan, save our rural hospitals; end the practice of prior authorization.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on lowering the cost of living, from electricity prices to housing to groceries, and on bringing people together to solve local problems.
Lists health care, cost of living, data centers, housing, veterans, farmers, infrastructure, and jobs as the policy areas she is most passionate about.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office found. Her campaign website (priorities and media pages) lists topic headings only; positions and statements are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and a 2026 press statement. No statements found on most other guide issues.
